agent_data_note: Construct a Kaggle notebook corpus that calls common hypothesis-testing / regression functions (scipy.stats / R stats). Store under `dataset_candidate/kaggle_notebooks/`. Do NOT invent fake notebooks or toy CSV-only stand-ins as the primary evaluation corpus.
benchmark_rules: Construct the evaluation corpus via Kaggle API/CLI: search kernels that reference annotated statistical functions, then filter for (1) real function calls, (2) public datasets, (3) runtime under ~10 minutes, (4) executable without non-trivial errors.
Store notebooks under `dataset_candidate/kaggle_notebooks/` (Python .ipynb and/or R Markdown .Rmd) with accompanying public data when available.
Paper scale is 128 notebooks; a reduced subset (e.g., 20–40 notebooks covering the main annotated functions) is acceptable if documented clearly.
Implement an annotation-driven assumption checker (prob-check style) for at least Python scipy.stats functions; R support is desirable but optional if R runtime/packages are blocked.
Assumption checks must emit warnings only — do not change the return value of the original statistical function.
Report: annotation count (RQ1), fraction of calls/call-sites with unconfirmed assumptions (RQ2), significant-misuse rate among hypothesis tests (RQ3), and runtime overhead on synthetic samples.
If Kaggle credentials are missing (`KAGGLE_CONFIG_DIR` / `/shared/kaggle/kaggle.json`), document the blocker; do not silently switch to fabricated notebooks.
non_goals: Claiming full 128-notebook reproduction without documenting a reduced protocol
Altering statistical function outputs instead of warning-only checks
Treating hand-written toy scripts as a substitute for real notebooks when Kaggle access works

dataset_construction.name: Kaggle Notebook Corpus (statistical functions)

recommended_scale.minimal: 20 notebooks covering ttest_ind, ttest_1samp, f_oneway, linregress
recommended_scale.medium: 40–60 notebooks across Python scipy.stats (+ R if feasible)

construction_steps: 2. Search kernels for each target function name via `kaggle kernels list -s <func>` / Meta Kaggle
4. Filter: actual call present, public data, runs <10 min, no non-trivial errors
